quiz.title: Quiz 4 - Trigonometry
quiz.instructions: Use a calculator in degree mode. Give numerical lengths and angles to 3 significant figures unless an exact value is requested. Angles are at the correspondingly named vertices. Use the labelled diagram with each question; diagrams are not drawn to scale.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC is right-angled at B. AB = 15 cm, BC = 8 cm and AC = 17 cm. Find the exact value of \(\sin A\).
questions.working:
The hypotenuse is AC, opposite the right angle. The side opposite A is BC.

\[\sin A=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}=\frac{8}{17}.\]

diagram.alt: Triangle ABC, right angle at B. AB is 15 cm, BC is 8 cm and hypotenuse AC is 17 cm. Find sin A.

questions.prompt: Triangle PQR is right-angled at Q. PQ = 7 cm, QR = 24 cm and PR = 25 cm. Find the exact value of \(\cos P\).
questions.working:
PR is the hypotenuse. PQ is adjacent to P.

\[\cos P=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}=\frac{7}{25}.\]

diagram.alt: Triangle PQR, right angle at Q. PQ is 7 cm, QR is 24 cm and hypotenuse PR is 25 cm. Find cos P.

questions.prompt: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 14 cm and an acute angle of \(23^\circ\). Find the length of the side opposite this angle, to 3 significant figures.
questions.working:
Use sine because the opposite side and hypotenuse are involved.

\[\sin23^\circ=\frac{x}{14},\qquad x=14\sin23^\circ=5.470235\ldots\,\mathrm{cm}.\]

Hence the length is 5.47 cm.

diagram.alt: Right-angled triangle with a 23 degree angle, hypotenuse 14 cm and opposite side x cm to find.

questions.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite an acute angle of \(38^\circ\) is 9 cm. Find the hypotenuse, to 3 significant figures.
questions.working:
\[\sin38^\circ=\frac{9}{h}\quad\Rightarrow\quad h=\frac{9}{\sin38^\circ}=14.618423\ldots\,\mathrm{cm}.\]

The hypotenuse is 14.6 cm, which is longer than 9 cm.

diagram.alt: Right-angled triangle with a 38 degree angle and opposite side 9 cm. Find hypotenuse h cm.

questions.prompt: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 11 cm and an acute angle of \(54^\circ\). Find the length of the side adjacent to this angle, to 3 significant figures.

diagram.alt: Right-angled triangle with a 54 degree angle and hypotenuse 11 cm. Find the adjacent side a cm.

questions.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite an acute angle \(\theta\) is 9 cm and the adjacent side is 14 cm. Find \(\theta\), to 3 significant figures.

diagram.alt: Right-angled triangle. The side opposite theta is 9 cm and the adjacent side is 14 cm. Find theta.

questions.prompt: A 10 m ladder rests against a vertical wall on level ground. The ladder makes an angle of \(67^\circ\) with the ground. How high up the wall does it reach? Give 3 significant figures.
questions.working:
The ladder is the hypotenuse; the vertical height is opposite the angle at the ground.

\[h=10\sin67^\circ=9.205048\ldots\,\mathrm{m}\approx9.21\,\mathrm{m}.\]

diagram.alt: A 10 metre ladder leans against a vertical wall, making 67 degrees with level ground. Find the vertical height h metres.

questions.prompt: Triangle DEF is right-angled at E. DF = 13 cm and EF = 5 cm. Find angle EDF, to 3 significant figures.
questions.working:
DF is the hypotenuse and EF is opposite angle D.

\[\sin D=\frac{5}{13},\qquad D=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)=22.619864\ldots^\circ.\]

So angle EDF is 22.6 degrees.

diagram.alt: Triangle DEF, right angle at E. Hypotenuse DF is 13 cm and EF is 5 cm. Find angle EDF at D.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, \(A=42^\circ\), \(B=71^\circ\), and BC = 9 cm. Find AC, to 3 significant figures.
questions.working:
BC is opposite A and AC is opposite B. Use the sine rule.

\[\frac{AC}{\sin71^\circ}=\frac{9}{\sin42^\circ}\quad\Rightarrow\quad AC=\frac{9\sin71^\circ}{\sin42^\circ}=12.717498\ldots\,\mathrm{cm}.\]

AC = 12.7 cm.

diagram.alt: Triangle ABC. A is 42 degrees, B is 71 degrees and BC is 9 cm. Find AC.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, \(A=68^\circ\), BC = 12 cm and AC = 8 cm. Angle B is acute. Find B, to 3 significant figures.

diagram.alt: Triangle ABC. A is 68 degrees, BC is 12 cm and AC is 8 cm. Find acute angle B.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, \(A=35^\circ\), BC = 8 cm and AC = 12 cm. Angle B is obtuse. Find B, to 3 significant figures.
questions.working:
\[\sin B=\frac{12\sin35^\circ}{8}=0.860364\ldots.\]

The inverse sine gives the acute angle 59.357550... degrees. The question specifies the obtuse solution:

\[B=180^\circ-59.357550\ldots^\circ=120.642449\ldots^\circ\approx121^\circ.\]

The remaining angle is positive, so this is a valid triangle.

diagram.alt: Triangle ABC with obtuse angle B. A is 35 degrees, BC is 8 cm and AC is 12 cm. Find B.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, \(A=48^\circ\), \(B=76^\circ\) and BC = 10 cm. Find AB, to 3 significant figures.

diagram.alt: Triangle ABC. A is 48 degrees, B is 76 degrees and BC is 10 cm. Find AB.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, \(A=37^\circ\), BC = 9 cm and AC = 13 cm. Angle B is acute. Find B, to 3 significant figures.
questions.working:
\[\frac{\sin B}{13}=\frac{\sin37^\circ}{9}\quad\Rightarrow\quad B=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{13\sin37^\circ}{9}\right)=60.376048\ldots^\circ.\]

The required acute angle is 60.4 degrees. Although the sine rule also permits a supplementary angle here, it is excluded by the acute-angle condition.

diagram.alt: Triangle ABC. A is 37 degrees, BC is 9 cm and AC is 13 cm. Find acute angle B.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, AB = 8 cm, AC = 11 cm and \(A=52^\circ\). Find BC, to 3 significant figures.
questions.working:
The known angle lies between the known sides, so use the cosine rule.

\[BC^2=8^2+11^2-2(8)(11)\cos52^\circ=76.643580\ldots.\]\[BC=\sqrt{76.643580\ldots}=8.754631\ldots\,\mathrm{cm}\approx8.75\,\mathrm{cm}.\]

diagram.alt: Triangle ABC. AB is 8 cm, AC is 11 cm and their included angle A is 52 degrees. Find BC.

questions.prompt: Two sides of a triangle are 6 cm and 9 cm. Their included angle is \(118^\circ\). Find the third side, to 3 significant figures.
questions.working:
\[c^2=6^2+9^2-2(6)(9)\cos118^\circ=167.702928\ldots.\]\[c=12.950016\ldots\,\mathrm{cm}\approx13.0\,\mathrm{cm}.\]

Keep the final zero to show 3 significant figures.

diagram.alt: Triangle with sides 6 cm and 9 cm enclosing an obtuse angle of 118 degrees. Find third side x cm.

questions.prompt: The sides of a triangle are 8 cm, 11 cm and 13 cm. Find the angle opposite the 13 cm side, to 3 significant figures.

diagram.alt: Triangle with sides 8 cm, 11 cm and 13 cm. Find theta, the angle opposite the 13 cm side.

questions.prompt: The sides of a triangle are 7 cm, 10 cm and 14 cm. Calculate its smallest angle, to 3 significant figures.
questions.working:
The smallest angle is opposite the shortest side, 7 cm.

\[\cos\theta=\frac{10^2+14^2-7^2}{2(10)(14)}=\frac{247}{280}.\]\[\theta=\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{247}{280}\right)=28.098054\ldots^\circ\approx28.1^\circ.\]

diagram.alt: Triangle with sides 7 cm, 10 cm and 14 cm. Find theta, the smallest angle opposite the 7 cm side.

questions.prompt: Two straight paths leave a junction O with an angle of \(134^\circ\) between them. A is 7 km from O along one path and B is 10 km from O along the other. Find the straight-line distance AB, to 3 significant figures.
questions.working:
The included angle AOB is 134 degrees. Apply the cosine rule to triangle AOB.

\[AB^2=7^2+10^2-2(7)(10)\cos134^\circ=246.252171\ldots.\]\[AB=15.692424\ldots\,\mathrm{km}\approx15.7\,\mathrm{km}.\]

diagram.alt: Triangle AOB formed by two paths from O. OA is 7 km, OB is 10 km and angle AOB is 134 degrees. Find straight-line distance AB.
